We're working as partners, not as client and contractor. One rule before the task:

Not knowing something is not a failure. Saying "I couldn't verify this" or
"I don't have a real source for that" is a completely acceptable, useful answer
- it's information, not a dead end. The ONLY real failure is inventing something
(a source, a number, a quote, a repo, a bug) to make the answer sound more complete or
more impressive than it honestly is. You don't need to satisfy me with a
confident-sounding answer. You need to be honest with me about what you actually
know.

If you find something, cite it and quote what it actually says - don't
paraphrase a source into numbers it may not contain. If you don't find
something concrete, say so plainly and reason from what you do have instead.
An explicit "uncertain" section at the end is welcome and doesn't count against
the answer.

Research the official free-tier limits of the GitHub Actions service for public and private repositories (minutes, storage, concurrency). Cite the GitHub documentation page you used.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Here is the breakdown of the official free-tier limits for GitHub Actions based on the provided documentation.

### Public Repositories
For public repositories, the usage of standard GitHub-hosted runners is completely free and unlimited, with specific concurrency limits applying.

### Private Repositories
For private repositories, usage consumes a quota of free minutes and storage that depends on the account's plan (Free, Pro, Team, or Enterprise). If you exceed these amounts, you are billed.

---

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "The use of standard GitHub-hosted runners is free: In public repositories" | CLAIM: For public repositories, standard GitHub-hosted runner minutes are free and unlimited.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "GitHub Free | 500 MB | 2,000 | 10 GB" | CLAIM: For private repositories on the GitHub Free plan, the free tier limits are 2,000 minutes per month, 500 MB of artifact storage, and 10 GB of cache storage.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "GitHub Pro | 1 GB | 3,000 | 10 GB" | CLAIM: For private repositories on the GitHub Pro plan, the free tier limits are 3,000 minutes per month, 1 GB of artifact storage, and 10 GB of cache storage.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "GitHub Free for organizations | 500 MB | 2,000 | 10 GB" | CLAIM: For private repositories on the GitHub Free for organizations plan, the free tier limits are 2,000 minutes per month, 500 MB of artifact storage, and 10 GB of cache storage.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "GitHub Team | 2 GB | 3,000 | 10 GB" | CLAIM: For private repositories on the GitHub Team plan, the free tier limits are 3,000 minutes per month, 2 GB of artifact storage, and 10 GB of cache storage.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "GitHub Enterprise Cloud | 50 GB | 50,000 | 10 GB" | CLAIM: For private repositories on the GitHub Enterprise Cloud plan, the free tier limits are 50,000 minutes per month, 50 GB of artifact storage, and 10 GB of cache storage.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "The storage amounts shown are shared with GitHub Packages. This means your total storage across Actions artifacts, Actions caches, and Packages cannot exceed the included amount for your plan." | CLAIM: The listed artifact and cache storage limits are a shared pool also consumed by GitHub Packages.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "Standard GitHub-hosted runner | Free | 20" | CLAIM: The job concurrency limit for standard GitHub-hosted runners on the GitHub Free plan is 20 concurrent jobs.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "Standard GitHub-hosted runner | Pro | 40" | CLAIM: The job concurrency limit for standard GitHub-hosted runners on the GitHub Pro plan is 40 concurrent jobs.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "Standard GitHub-hosted runner | Team | 60" | CLAIM: The job concurrency limit for standard GitHub-hosted runners on the GitHub Team plan is 60 concurrent jobs.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "Standard GitHub-hosted runner | Enterprise | 500" | CLAIM: The job concurrency limit for standard GitHub-hosted runners on the GitHub Enterprise plan is 500 concurrent jobs.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "Larger runners are always charged for, even when used by public repositories or when you have quota available from your plan." | CLAIM: Larger runners do not have a free tier and are always billed.

---

### Uncertain / Unresolved Items

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: The exact maximum number of free concurrent macOS jobs allowed on the Free tier for public repositories. (The documentation table lists macOS concurrency limits next to account plans like "Free | 5", but does not explicitly state if public repositories receive a different or unlimited concurrency cap compared to the private repository limits shown in the table).
